Jacobs Greenhouse Gas and Institute of Paper Science and Technology (2006). Pulp and Paper Industry Energy Bandwidth Study. Report for the American Institute of Chemical Engineers (AIChE), prepared by Jacobs (Greenville, South Carolina) and IPST at Georgia Institute of Technology (Atlanta), Project Number 16CX8700, August 2006 (authors R.B. Kinstrey, Jacobs, and D. White, IPST). OSTI 1218635. No DOI printed.

Locators are PRINTED page numbers (footer "Project: 16CX8700 N"; PDF page = printed + 1). Basis: U.S. 2002 (MECS 2002 energy distributed over AF&PA 2002 production), short tons (stated p.15; figures label pulp "adt"/"adst" and paper "mdt" loosely, numbers equal the per-ton tables). Loaded: (1) powerhouse boiler efficiencies current vs BAT (Tables 4.1, 6.2); (2) electricity, steam and direct fuel per short ton for 11 pulping routes, market pulp and 17 paper grades, current (Table 4.5) and BAT (Table 6.1) as _efficiency-base and _bat variants; (3) Tab H area-average energy (steam+electricity+direct fuel) for wood prep, cooking, evaporation, chemical prep/kiln, bleaching, mechanical refining, recycling, paper wet end, pressing and drying for current/BAT/practical minimum (PM -> _efficiency-strong, only where PM differs from BAT: evaporation, kiln, paper drying); (4) the three bandwidth areas in detail: paper drying 4.2/3.0/1.3 MMBtu/fst, black liquor evaporation 3.5/3.0/2.2 MMBtu/adst, lime kiln per ADt pulp 1.93/1.66/1.38/0.90 and per short ton of lime (Table 8.2); (5) Sect. 7 modern-mill numbers (digesters, O2 delignification, ECF bleaching electricity, 4- and 7-effect evaporators, recovery boiler and gasifier electrical efficiencies, forming, drying, tissue) with descriptions of emerging options. Not loaded to main: theoretical minima (physical floor) and sector totals (other-values), figure bar charts without printed labels, Figs 4.6-4.8/6.7-6.9 mill diagrams (area values taken from Tab H instead), Tab A/B production and reference data, Tabs C-F (workbook pointers only), water measures. No capex or opex anywhere in the report. OVERLAP: doe_2015_003 (DOE 2015, Energetics) is the 2010-basis successor with the same CT/SOA/PM convention (evaporator CT 3.55 vs 3.5 here, SOA 3.04 vs 3.0, PM 2.27 vs 2.2; kiln CT 2.07 MMBtu/ton vs Tab H 2.63; cooking 2.44 vs 2.80); the 2015 study uses onsite energy per short ton of chemical pulp while this report uses 2002 MECS. Kramer 2009 (kramer_2009_001) reprinted the BAT columns of Table 6.1 (Table E.1, via NCASI 2009) in GJ/t and loaded them as final energy; Table 6.1 here is the original source. TRAPS: (a) Sect. 8 text gives the evaporation practical minimum as "2.2 MMBtu/bdst" and cites Table 8.5, but Table 8.4 (adst) is the practical-minimum table; (b) the kiln "practical minimum" 0.90 MMBtu/adt is 35% below the BAT bar, but the text also says Jaakko Poyry numbers would give only 14%; (c) the "fst" unit of the drying bandwidth is not defined; (d) mixed unit labels adt/adst/ADmt and GJ vs MMBtu inside Sect. 7 (both printed values were kept in notes); (e) SGW energy rises from 8.04 to 8.99 MMBtu/t in the BAT table (printed so); (f) the lime kiln mud-solids saving is printed as 44 MJ/t lime and as "0.4 MMBtu/adst" in the same sentence; (g) Table 4.1 uses "Other" in MECS Table 3.2 differently from AF&PA Table 3.4; (h) practical-minimum cases change only paper drying, evaporation and lime kiln direct fuel, so PM equals BAT elsewhere. Heating-value basis is never stated; electricity converted at 3,412 Btu/kWh (p.12).
